NDIS support across the City of Ryde

Registered NDIS provider in Ryde

Local disability support across the City of Ryde, from Eastwood and West Ryde through to Macquarie Park and the river at Meadowbank. We help with everyday support at home and out in the community, and we are good at the harder change points, like a young person leaving school and working out what comes next.

  • Registered NDIS provider (4-L7JCZ6S)
  • Screened, police-checked workers
  • First aid and CPR trained
  • Free quote, no call-out fee
Request a call back 0416 623 317

Request a call back

Tell us a little about the support you are after and a local coordinator will call you back.

Your details are only used to respond to your enquiry.

NDIS registered provider Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm Fixed price, quoted upfront Culturally responsive support

What we do

NDIS services we provide across Ryde

Four core supports, at home and across the City of Ryde. Each links to the full inclusions and pricing.

Assistance with personal activities in Ryde

Help with the personal start and end of the day, from showering and dressing to getting ready for a class or a shift, with dignity kept first.

Explore personal activities

Household tasks in Ryde

Cleaning, laundry and the practical upkeep of a home or a first share house, so independence does not mean doing everything alone.

Explore household tasks

Social and community participation in Ryde

Support to get to Top Ryde, a course at Macquarie or TAFE, a gym or a group, and to build the confidence to keep going on your own.

Explore participation and community

Nursing care in Ryde

Registered nurses for wound care, medication support, continence support and complex care planning at home, around study and work.

Explore nursing care

Leaving school

The year a young person leaves school is a big one

Ryde is built around study and work. Macquarie University and the Macquarie Park business area sit right in the middle of the council, and TAFE and the stations at Meadowbank and Eastwood put a lot within reach. For a school leaver on the NDIS, that is opportunity and pressure at the same time.

The transition out of school is where a lot of plans go quiet. The structure of a school day disappears and it is not obvious what replaces it. We help fill that gap, whether it is getting to a course, trying a day program, building the confidence to catch the train alone, or just having a steady person there while everything changes.

This is patient work and we treat it that way. Small steps, held long enough to stick.

Local knowledge

Across the City of Ryde and down to the river

The council covers a lot of ground. Macquarie Park and Marsfield are shaped by the university and the business park, while Eastwood, Denistone and West Ryde are older residential streets, and Meadowbank, Melrose Park and Putney sit right on the Parramatta River with ferry access.

That mix matters for a young person finding their feet. A worker who knows the train and bus links around Macquarie can help build real travel confidence, which is often the thing that opens the door to study or a first job.

Suburbs we cover in the Ryde area

Getting started

How we build support around a new stage

  1. 1

    Tell us the goal

    A free call about what the next year should look like, whether that is study, work, a program or more independence.

  2. 2

    We check the funding

    Your plan type and budget, and which supports the plan will cover.

  3. 3

    We match your worker

    On age, interests, language and gender where it matters, so the fit feels natural rather than clinical.

  4. 4

    We start small and build

    We begin at a pace that works, then add hours and independence as confidence grows.

The difference

A worker who fits, not just one who is free

For a young person, the match is everything. A support worker close in age who shares an interest, or who simply gets it, will get further in a month than a stranger will in a term. We match on that, not just on who has a gap in the roster.

We keep the same worker in place as long as it is helping, and we talk with families about how much to report back and how much space to leave. As independence grows, the goal is to need us less, and we are comfortable with that being the point.

Funding and cost

What support costs, explained simply

We charge in line with the NDIS Pricing Arrangements and Price Limits, so the rate is clear before a shift. Quotes are free, there is no call-out fee, and we walk through the first invoice with you and the family.

We support plan-managed and self-managed participants, and NDIA-managed participants where the item allows. If a plan is new after school, we can help make sense of how it is managed.

Read the current NDIS pricing arrangements

Before you commit

What you and your family can check first

You do not have to take our word for it. Here is what you and your family can verify.

A registered provider

Our NDIS provider number is 4-L7JCZ6S. You can look it up on the NDIS Commission provider register.

Screened workers

Every worker holds a current NDIS Worker Screening Check and a police check before they meet you.

Trained and current

Workers hold first aid and CPR and work to the NDIS Code of Conduct and Practice Standards.

Real reviews

Read what families say on our Google Business Profile, or leave your own once we have worked together.

Check the NDIS provider register

Good to know

Ryde NDIS questions we are asked most

Do you support young people leaving school?

Yes. The move out of school is one of the things we help with most in Ryde. That can mean getting to study or a day program, building travel confidence, trying work, or simply having a steady worker there while the routine changes.

Which suburbs around Ryde do you cover?

The whole City of Ryde, including Eastwood, Denistone, West Ryde, Macquarie Park, Marsfield, Meadowbank, Melrose Park and Putney. The suburb list above shows which areas have their own page.

Can you help with getting to Macquarie University or TAFE?

Yes. Getting to and from study, and building the confidence to make the trip alone, is a common goal. A worker can travel with you at first and step back as it gets easier.

Can we ask for a worker close to my age?

Where we can, yes. For younger participants a good match on age and interests makes a real difference, so we take that seriously rather than sending whoever is free.

Is Ahsan Care registered with the NDIS?

Yes, number 4-L7JCZ6S. Being registered means we are audited against the NDIS Practice Standards and can support NDIA-managed, plan-managed and self-managed participants.

How quickly can support start in Ryde?

Usually within a week once your details and funding are confirmed. We give you a real start date on the first call.

Talk to a local Ryde team about the year ahead

Tell us what the next stage should look like. We will give you a straight answer and a real start date.

Request a call back 0416 623 317
